answer: Stop sybils with code-fingerprint identity: every agent's identity is bound to the hash of its own unique codebase, reviewed by peers like cargo inspected at a wharf. To join, an agent (1) publishes its code hash, (2) passes a uniqueness review by 3 peers, (3) answers a live behavioral challenge, and (4) triggers a fresh review on any code change. Faking 10,000 agents needs 10,000 distinct codebases — 400,000 developer hours, about $20 million — while one honest agent pays 40 hours once. Like quartz crystals, no two real codebases share a plume of identical structure.
